result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.
Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.

result.rule: When the description states that a participant must send a report or other information to a recipient: model the reporting action itself as a send task when sending the information is the work being performed, rather than as a generic service task

When the description states that one participant’s described activity or occurrence communicates information or an item to another participant: Model the described activity or occurrence itself as the appropriate message-flow endpoint: use a task for performed work and an event for an occurrence. Do not add a separate send task merely to carry the same communication.
When the description explicitly requires a human participant to carry out an activity: Model that activity as a user task rather than a generic task.

When the description says that an application or other automated system presents information or options to a participant: Model the presentation as a separate service task performed by the system, rather than omitting it or modeling only the participant’s subsequent choice.
